A1.justification: Both PDFs describe vCache, with matching algorithms, core equations, and correctness theorem. Their text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original cache evaluations on classification, chatbot, and search workloads, plus runtime experiments and component ablations in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds mixed-workload and OpenAI embedding evaluations, empirical sigmoid diagnostics, and computation-latency measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same cache updates, per-embedding logistic estimation, confidence adjustment, and randomized exploration policy. The new evaluations and explanations do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The three existing benchmarks remain. SemCacheCombo adds a controlled mixture containing deliberately non-reusable prompts, extending scenarios within existing domains. Its precise composition is inconsistent: Section 5 names SearchQueries plus LMArena, whereas Appendix H.4 specifies Classification plus LMArena.

E2.justification: The GPTCache and fine-tuned embedding comparisons, evaluated GS/GD/LD1/LD2 variants in Table 3, and vLLM comparison in Table 2 are retained. The added evaluations reuse GPTCache rather than introduce another comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: v5 adds an LMArena configuration using text-embedding-3-small with GPT-4.1-nano, a shuffled 27,500-prompt Combo evaluation, and diagnostic selection of the two most-observed cached embeddings. Existing benchmark sizes, metrics, and threshold/error-bound sweep procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 substantially expands supporting analyses through direct sigmoid-assumption diagnostics at per-embedding and aggregate levels (Appendix E), the mixed non-reusable-prompt test, and exploration-probability computation latency versus stream size (Appendix F.4). The earlier component ablations and threshold-distribution analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The new diagnostics introduce statistical estimation through k=5 nearest-neighbor smoothing and binned correctness proportions; the latency analysis adds a fitted trend. Existing 95% Wallis confidence-interval reporting is unchanged, and neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seed lists.

E6.justification: The matched original benchmark panels and Tables 2–4 retain their results. v5 adds complete Combo and OpenAI-configuration comparisons plus diagnostic and timing findings. Appendix F.2 reports up to 12.5× higher hit rates on Combo, while F.3 reports up to 26× lower error at matched latency on OpenAI LMArena. These are new-setting results, not same-setting method improvements; Section 5 inconsistently attributes the 12.5× result to LMArena.

T1.justification: New Appendix D argues an O(1/sqrt(n_y)) convergence rate for per-embedding maximum-likelihood estimates and derived policy quantities under standard logistic-regression regularity assumptions, invoking the delta method. The original definitions, Theorem 4.1, and Appendix C proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The headline performance claims increase from the introduction's 2× higher hit rates and 6× lower errors to 12.5× and 26×, and the benchmark contribution increases from three to four. The central contribution of online per-embedding caching with user-defined error guarantees remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds model-choice reasoning based on monotonicity, boundedness, and low parameter count, interpreting the new diagnostics as support for sigmoid modeling. Appendix F.4 adds an interpretation of negligible, stable computation overhead. The existing limitations concerning response judging, i.i.d. inputs, and sigmoid assumptions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H.4 documents Combo's class selection, component counts, and shuffling, alongside new model and diagnostic settings. The reproducibility statement largely consolidates existing disclosures. Conversely, the revised displays omit the static-threshold values explicitly supplied in v4's Figures 4 and 7.

R1.justification: v5 adds a reference for text-embedding-3-small documentation. Section 2 and the positioning against static thresholds, embedding fine-tuning, and earlier threshold-learning approaches remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 adds ethics and reproducibility statements, updates author and conference-header text, reorders evaluation material, and reorganizes appendices around the added analyses. Most existing narrative and method prose is retained, making the editorial restructuring limited.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 expand from two-row displays to five-row composites, incorporating v4's SearchQueries Figures 7–8 and two added evaluation configurations. New Figures 7–9 display sigmoid diagnostics and timing. These changes substantially reorganize the results presentation; existing tables and benchmark illustrations are also relocated.

improvement.justification: The added model configuration, mixed workload, and sigmoid diagnostics provide useful validation beyond v4, yielding a limited overall improvement. The gain is constrained by sparse per-embedding diagnostics and reporting defects: Section 5 and Appendix H.4 disagree on Combo's sources, and Figure 9 contains latency measurements exceeding the claimed 1.5 ms maximum.
